newsitem.title: USA: N.J. pension bond cut to $2.75 bln from $2.9 bln.
newsitem.headline: N.J. pension bond cut to $2.75 bln from $2.9 bln.

text.p: A shrunken version of New Jersey Gov. Christie Whitman's pension bond issue will be put to the state Senate Monday after a full day of bargaining got it through a key committee of the state Senate last night.
The Senate Budget and Appropriations Committee voted 4-3 to approve the proposal after several changes.

Stymied by the opposition of organized labor, the administration agreed to reduce the borrowing to $2.75 billion from $2.9 billion. That will lessen the $647 million in relief to the governor's current budget proposal, but excess revenues will more than cover it, administration sources say.

Among the concessions Whitman made were to reduce pension contributions by state workers for two years, to find other state jobs for displaced workers and to shelve her proposal to sell the state-owned temporary disability insurance plan.
The Philadelphia Inquirer reported Friday that the typical state employee, making $43,000, will save $215 each year.
The Thursday morning meeting of the Senate Budget Committee was delayed by 10 hours of intense negotiations.

Setting the scene for the showdown was Whitman's past success in bargaining with the more than 50,000 unionized state workers. She obtained a two-year wage freeze in July 1995 and increased the pension contribution of most workers. She also has reduced the work force by nearly 2,000 jobs and plans to eliminate another 2,000 jobs in the coming fiscal year, mostly by closing two state psychiatric hospitals.
